classification.difficultyReason: Calculate missing angles where necessary, then use equal angles to identify equal sides.

content.prompt: Determine whether $\triangle ABC$ in each part is an isosceles triangle, naming the equal sides. Give reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above BC; both base angles are labelled 58 degrees. No equality ticks.
spec.mathematics: Angles ABC and ACB are each 58 degrees.

answer.worked: The angles at $B$ and $C$ are equal. The sides opposite equal angles are equal, so $AB=AC$. Hence $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles.

spec.description: Right triangle ABC, with A vertically above C, angle B labelled 38 degrees and a right-angle square at C.
spec.mathematics: Angle B is 38 degrees and angle C is 90 degrees.

answer.short: Not isosceles: its angles are $38^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $52^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=180^\circ-90^\circ-38^\circ\\\angle BAC&=52^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$. All three angles are different, so no two sides are equal. The triangle is not isosceles.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above BC, angle A labelled 52 degrees and angle B labelled 64 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Angle A is 52 degrees and angle B is 64 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Angle C and equal sides are not supplied.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-52^\circ-64^\circ\\\angle ACB&=64^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$. Since $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$, their opposite sides are equal: $AB=AC$. Hence the triangle is isosceles.

spec.description: Obtuse triangle ABC with C between the unlabelled leftward base extension and B; A is upper left.
spec.mathematics: The exterior angle at C is 72 degrees; the interior angle at B is 36 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two source angle givens are visible.

answer.worked:
An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CAB+36^\circ&=72^\circ\\\angle CAB&=36^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $\angle CAB=\angle ABC$, the opposite sides are equal: $BC=AC$. Hence the triangle is isosceles.

spec.description: Left-pointing triangle ABC, A vertically above C; BA extends beyond A.
spec.mathematics: Interior angle B is 66 degrees. Exterior angle at A, between AC and the extension of BA, is 142 degrees.

answer.short: Not isosceles: $\angle A=38^\circ$, $\angle B=66^\circ$ and $\angle C=76^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=180^\circ-142^\circ\\\angle BAC&=38^\circ\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of a triangle,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BCA&=180^\circ-38^\circ-66^\circ\\\angle BCA&=76^\circ\end{align*}$$
All three angles are different, so the triangle is not isosceles.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above and left of C, and BC extended right beyond C.
spec.mathematics: Interior angle B is 37 degrees and exterior angle C is 112 degrees.

answer.short: Not isosceles: $\angle A=75^\circ$, $\angle B=37^\circ$ and $\angle C=68^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-112^\circ\\\angle ACB&=68^\circ\end{align*}$$
The exterior angle equals the sum of the opposite interior angles.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC+37^\circ&=112^\circ\\\angle BAC&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
All three angles are different, so the triangle is not isosceles.
